cases.note: The verifier's own policy, which it had to state to get: max_age has no default.

Enforced even with max_age=None: expires is the SIGNER's declaration, and a verifier that accepts one without checking it is selling a guarantee nobody bought.
65536 is not a port, so @authority cannot be built: a base that cannot be built is a signature mismatch (profile section 9).
Nothing but :port may follow an IP-literal's closing bracket.
An IP-literal holds an IPv6 address or IPvFuture (RFC 3986 section 3.2.2). The signature is good over the base a port without that check would build.
65536 behind 5,000 leading zeros is still out of range, and is refused without converting the digits.

The identity point: under it a signature of 0x01 and 63 zero bytes verifies over any message, so it is refused before the signature is examined.

R carries a point of order 8. [8][S]B = [8]R + [8][k]A holds and [S]B = R + [k]A does not, so the cofactorless check fiki pins refuses it (RFC 8032 section 5.1.7).
The key is SEED_A's plus a point of order 8, and k is not a multiple of 8, so only the cofactored equation holds.
